title: A Botswana Mobile Safari With Friends: Crew, Campsites and How the Costs Split
meta_title: Botswana Mobile Safari With Friends: A Group Planner
meta_description: Plan a Botswana mobile safari with friends: route through Moremi, Khwai and Savuti, best months, vehicles, tents and how group costs split.
excerpt: A Botswana mobile safari lets a group of friends move a private tented camp through Moremi, Khwai and Savuti. Here is how the route, crew, vehicles and costs work.
content:
A Botswana mobile safari is a guided camping trip where a crew moves a private tented camp between Moremi, Khwai and Savuti while you spend each day on game drives. For a group of friends it is the most sociable way to see northern Botswana: one vehicle, one campfire and a wild camp that belongs only to you.

The planning is where friends' groups get stuck. Who books the campsites, how many vehicles do you need, what does "fully serviced" really include, and how does the bill split fairly? This guide answers those questions from our Nairobi office, and when you are ready, our team builds the trip through our special occasion and friends' safaris service, whether you are marking a birthday or just finally doing the trip you talked about for years.

Quick Facts

  • Classic route: Maun to Moremi, the Khwai area and Savuti, ending in Maun or Kasane
  • Ideal length: 6 to 9 nights, with two nights at each campsite
  • Best months: June to October for game; May and November as shoulder months
  • Group size: 4 to about 16 friends, adding a vehicle and crew for larger groups
  • Camp style: Dome tents with bedding, a dining tent, bucket showers and camp toilets
  • Malaria: Risk in Chobe and Ngamiland, highest November to June (NHS Fit for Travel)
  • Children: Usually best for ages 8 and over, as camps are unfenced

What Is a Botswana Mobile Safari, Exactly?

A Botswana mobile safari is a road-based camping trip led by a professional guide, with a crew that drives ahead, pitches the tents and cooks. Every two or three nights the camp is struck and moved to the next wildlife area, so the group follows the game instead of returning to one fixed lodge.

The Botswana mobile safari grew up here because the best wildlife areas sit close together. Moremi Game Reserve, the Khwai community area on its northern edge and the Savuti region of Chobe National Park form a natural chain, linked by sand tracks a 4x4 covers in half a day.

Fully serviced or participation?

There are two main styles. On a fully serviced Botswana mobile safari the crew does everything: pitching tents, making beds, cooking, washing up and heating water for showers. On a participation trip, usually cheaper and often in larger mixed groups, guests help put up their own tents and pitch in with chores.

For a private group of friends we nearly always recommend a fully serviced Botswana mobile safari. It costs more, but it frees every hour of daylight for game drives, and nobody spends the evening wrestling with a tent pole.

What the camp looks like

Our 7 Day Botswana Family Camping Safari through Moremi, Khwai and Savuti shows the standard set-up: walk-in dome tents with proper bedding, a shared dining area, camp toilets and bucket showers, and meals cooked fresh by a camp chef and served around the fire. The same camp works just as well for a group of friends as it does for families.

Why Camp With Friends Instead of Joining a Scheduled Group?

Camping privately with friends gives you control over the pace, the menu and the mood that a scheduled group trip cannot. You choose when to leave camp, how long to sit with a pride of lions and whether the evening ends early or runs late by the fire, without negotiating with strangers.

The vehicle is the biggest difference. On a shared departure you may sit with six strangers, some keen to move on while others want to wait for a leopard. On a Botswana mobile safari with friends, the group sets the rules and the guide tailors drives to photographers, birders or first-timers.

A private Botswana mobile safari also makes a celebration easy. The crew can bake a cake in a camp oven or set up a sundowner on a quiet floodplain for a milestone birthday.

If your group is still deciding on style and dates, our group safaris page explains how we plan private trips for clubs, families and friends, and the step-by-step guide to organising a group safari walks the organiser through deposits, rooming lists and timelines.

Which Route Works Best for a Group of Friends?

The route that works best for most friends' groups is Maun, Moremi, Khwai and Savuti over six or seven nights, finishing in Kasane for the Chobe River or flying back from Maun. It strings together the delta's edge, a predator-rich community area and Savuti's elephant country with no backtracking.

DayAreaWhat the group does
1Maun to MoremiMeet the guide in Maun, drive about 100 km north (roughly four hours with game viewing), camp pitched on arrival
2Moremi Game ReserveMorning and afternoon drives around lagoons and floodplains, rest at camp at midday
3Moremi to KhwaiBreak camp after breakfast and drive north to the Khwai area, afternoon drive
4KhwaiA full day in a community area known for wild dogs, leopard and big elephant herds
5Khwai to SavutiRoughly 100 to 120 km of sand tracks, about four hours, with a picnic lunch on the way
6SavutiDrives around the Savuti Marsh and channel, famous for lions, hyenas and elephants
7Savuti to Maun or KasaneFinal drive out; Kasane is about 170 km and five to seven hours by road

Drive times are estimates. Deep sand, water after rain and a good sighting can all stretch a transfer, so on a Botswana mobile safari we never plan two long moves back to back.

Adding the Chobe River or the delta

Groups with nine or ten nights often add two nights on the Chobe riverfront at the end for a sunset boat cruise among elephants and hippos, or start with a fly-in lodge in the delta for mokoro trips. The 7 Day Botswana Celebration Safari through Chobe, Moremi and Khwai shows how a lodge-and-flights version of the same region works if some of your friends prefer a bed with solid walls.

For a wider look at how the delta and the river compare, our Chobe safari planning guide covers the riverfront and Savuti in more depth.

When Is the Best Time for a Botswana Mobile Safari?

The best time for a Botswana mobile safari is the dry season from June to October, when water shrinks to lagoons and channels, animals concentrate and the tracks are at their most reliable. Nights in June and July can drop close to freezing, while October is very hot, so pack for both ends.

SeasonMonthsWhat it means for a camping group
Early dryMay to JuneGreen bush drying out, cool nights, fewer vehicles and a good balance of game and comfort
Peak dryJuly to OctoberThe strongest game viewing; campsites book up first and October days are very hot
Early rainsNovemberFirst storms, newborn antelope and returning migrant birds; tracks still mostly fine
Green seasonDecember to AprilLush scenery and superb birding, but heat, storms, mud and more mosquitoes

Our best time to visit Botswana guide goes month by month. The short version: book a dry-season Botswana mobile safari a year ahead, or pick the shoulder months for quieter campsites.

How Do Group Size, Vehicles and Tents Work?

Group size on a Botswana mobile safari is set by the vehicles. Most open safari vehicles seat six or seven guests so that everyone has a good view, which means one vehicle for a small party and two or more for larger groups, each with its own guide and extra crew.

Group sizeVehiclesHow it usually runs
4 to 6 friends1 vehicleOne guide and a compact crew; everyone gets a window seat
7 to 12 friends2 vehiclesTwo guides who can split for different interests, then meet back at camp
13 to 16 friends2 to 3 vehiclesA larger crew and more tents; still one shared camp and one campfire
Over 163 or more vehiclesOften split into two camps a short drive apart to keep each one calm

Rooming in a mobile camp

Most friends share two to a tent, and solo travellers can have their own tent for a supplement. Tell us early if anyone snores or needs a tent near the toilet; a good rooming list is the quiet secret of a happy Botswana mobile safari.

How Much Does a Group Mobile Safari in Botswana Cost?

The cost of a Botswana mobile safari for a group depends mainly on group size, season and how fully serviced the camp is. Much of the cost is fixed, such as the vehicle, guide, crew and equipment, so the price per person falls as more friends fill each vehicle.

Cost itemHow it is chargedEffect of a bigger group
Vehicle, guide and crewPer day, per vehicleShared by more people, so cheaper per head until the vehicle is full
Camping equipment and foodPer person, per nightRoughly the same for each person
Campsite feesPer person, per night, paid to the campsite operatorRoughly the same for each person
Park entry feesPer person, per day, paid to the wildlife departmentRoughly the same for each person
Flights and chartersPer seat, or per aircraft for a charterA charter can work out well once a plane is full

Park fees are in flux. In February 2026 the government consulted on raising the non-resident daily park fee from P380 to P500, and later reports said the change had been postponed, so confirm the current rate when you ask for a quote (checked November 2026). The Botswana Daily News report on the proposed tourism user fees has the background.

Our group terms help a friends' trip too: for every six paying travellers the seventh place is free, each person can pay separately, and a deposit of 30 to 40 per cent holds the booking with the balance due two to four weeks before travel. Full terms are confirmed with your quote.

Booking Campsites, Permits and Paperwork

Booking is the part of a Botswana mobile safari that rewards an early start. The public campsites inside Moremi and Chobe are run by a handful of private concession holders, while park entry fees go to the Department of Wildlife and National Parks, and the two must line up before a group can enter.

In practice the campsite operators are paid first, then their vouchers are used to settle park fees. Popular sites in Moremi and Savuti have few pitches, so for a July to October Botswana mobile safari we start securing them about a year ahead and handle the whole chain for the organiser.

Visas and health

Visitors from many countries can enter Botswana without a visa; those who need one can apply through the Botswana government visitor visa page, which gives a processing time of 7 to 14 days (checked November 2026). Each traveller should check the rule for their own passport before booking flights.

NHS Fit for Travel lists the northern districts of Chobe and Ngamiland, which include Moremi, Khwai and Savuti, as the highest malaria risk areas, with risk year-round and highest from November to June. Antimalarial tablets are usually advised there, so everyone should see a travel clinic six to eight weeks before departure.

Insider Tips

  • Book the campsites first: Flights are easy to find; two nights at the right Moremi site is not
  • Pick one money person: Agree how drinks and tips are shared before you leave Maun
  • Pack soft bags: Vehicles and light aircraft have little space for hard suitcases
  • Bring layers: Dawn drives in June and July are cold, even when afternoons are warm
  • Bring power banks: Mobile camps have little or no mains power, so pack spare batteries and a car charger
  • Plan a rest morning: On a seven-night trip, one late breakfast in camp keeps the group fresh

Is a Botswana Mobile Safari Right for Your Group?

A Botswana mobile safari is right for friends who value wild nights and shared evenings over room service and swimming pools. It suits groups who are happy with bucket showers, early starts and unfenced camps, and who want the feeling of being the only people in the bush.

It is less suited to anyone needing mobility support, very young children or light sleepers. Mixed groups can still make it work with a lodge night at the start or end, and our Botswana safari guide for first-timers shows how the regions fit together if your group is still choosing.

Whatever the mix, a private Botswana mobile safari with friends is planned around the people in your group, so share ages, interests and any worries early and we will shape the route around them. For more Botswana trips and ideas, browse our Botswana safari packages.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people can join a private Botswana mobile safari?

A private Botswana mobile safari runs well for four to about sixteen friends. One vehicle and crew suits a small party, and larger groups add a second vehicle, more tents and more crew. Above sixteen, very large groups are often split into two camps to keep the wild feel.

Is a Botswana mobile safari safe?

A Botswana mobile safari is safe when you follow the guide's rules, even though the campsites are unfenced. Animals do walk through camp, so you stay inside the tent at night, use a torch after dark, never walk off alone and keep food out of tents. The guide briefs everyone on the first afternoon and the crew keeps watch around the fire.

What is the best month for a Botswana mobile safari?

The best months for a Botswana mobile safari are usually June to October, the dry season, when animals gather at permanent water in Moremi, Khwai and Savuti and the sand tracks are firm enough to move camp easily. May and November are good shoulder months. December to March is green, hot and wet, with lovely birding but harder driving.

Do we have to help put up the tents?

On a fully serviced Botswana mobile safari you do not have to help with the tents at all. The crew pitches and strikes camp, cooks every meal and heats water for bucket showers, so your days are spent on game drives. Cheaper participation trips ask guests to help with chores, which some friends' groups enjoy and others would rather skip.

Can we fly part of the way on a mobile safari in Botswana?

Yes, many groups fly part of a mobile safari in Botswana. A common plan is to fly from Maun into the delta for a lodge night or two, then join the mobile camp for the drive through Moremi, Khwai and Savuti. Light aircraft usually limit luggage to about 20 kg in soft bags, and a private charter can keep a whole group together.

Final Thoughts

A Botswana mobile safari gives a group of friends something lodges rarely can: a private camp in the middle of Moremi, Khwai and Savuti, with the same faces at the fire every night. Go fully serviced, travel in the dry months and book the campsites early, and the rest takes care of itself.
